references.alg-ho-absolute: Absolute value equals5 iff2x-3=5 or2x-3=-5. Thus exactlyx=4,-1; both substitute in the original.
references.alg-ho-range: A=(x-2)²-3. On[-1,4], x-2 lies in[-3,2], so its square ranges from0 to9. Minimum-3 atx2, maximum6 atx-1. The square bounds prove all interior points are covered.
references.alg-ho-remainder: By polynomial division/remainder theorem, x-2 divides P iffP(2)=8-8+2a+4=0, iff a=-2. Witha=-2, direct division givesP=(x-2)(x²-2).
references.alg-ho-sign: x=-2 is excluded. On x<-2 both numerator/denominator are negative; on(-2,1) signs differ; on[1,infinity) quotient is nonnegative. Exactly(-infinity,-2) union[1,infinity).
references.geo-ho-altitude: Pythagoras givesBC10. Similar right triangles giveAB²=BH·BC, AC²=CH·BC, soBH18/5, CH32/5. Area computed using perpendicular legs and baseBC givesAH=AB·AC/BC=24/5. Orthogonality and similarity, not a drawing, justify the relations.
references.geo-ho-chord: OA=OB=5, AM=BM=4 and OM shared imply trianglesOMA,OMB congruent by SSS. Equal adjacent angles atM total180°, so each90°. Pythagoras givesOM²=25-16=9; OM3.
references.geo-ho-cyclic: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum180°. DAB is the angle atA, BCD atC; C=180-110=70°.
references.geo-ho-ceva: Ceva applies to three concurrent cevians withD,E,F internal onBC,CA,AB. (BD/DC)(CE/EA)(AF/FB)=1; 2·3·ratio=1, soAF/FB=1/6.
references.nt-ho-cube: 18=2·3². For18n to be a cube, n must contain at least2² and3¹, hence n divisible by12. n12 gives18n216=6³, proving it is the least positive value. Prime-exponent congruences justify necessity.
references.nt-ho-between: Forn≥1, n²<n(n+1)<(n+1)². There is no integer square strictly between consecutive nonnegative squares. This proves impossibility for all positive n.
references.nt-ho-coprime: Any common positive divisor d divides3(2n+1)-2(3n+2)=-1, hence d1. Both numbers are positive for n≥0, so gcd1.
references.nt-ho-cycle: 10≡3 mod7. The nonzero residue sequence for3 powers is3,2,6,4,5,1, then repeats with period6. 2026=6·337+4, so remainder3⁴≡4. Show3⁶≡1 to justify repeating, not just sampled powers.
references.comb-ho-derangement: Label hats/people0,1,2. All six bijections are possible. No fixed points leaves exactly the two 3-cycles(1,2,0),(2,0,1). Case split by first recipient accounts for all possibilities once.
references.comb-ho-grid: Every path is an ordered word with3R,2U, so10 total. Paths through(1,1) have2 prefixes and3 suffixes, so6; concatenate is a bijection. Subtract to get4 avoiding paths.
references.comb-ho-dice: Thirty-six ordered pairs of face values are equiprobable. Exactly(1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) sum7. Probability6/36=1/6; order matters.
references.comb-ho-extremal: Partition1..10 into five chains by odd part: {1,2,4,8},{3,6},{5,10},{7},{9}. Six selected numbers force two in a chain; they differ by a positive power of2, so the larger is divisible by the smaller. The chains are disjoint and exhaustive.
